title: When I get home
goal: Say when, once and until something happens with -(y)IncA and -(y)IncAyA kadar: eve gelince, otobüs gelinceye kadar.

intro.text: Add `-(y)IncA` to a verb for **when** or **once**: *Eve gelince ararım* (When I get home, I'll call). It takes no person and no tense: the main verb gives both. Add the dative and *kadar* for **until**: *Sen gelinceye kadar bekleriz*.

vocab.en: to set off, to leave (on a journey)
break, rest stop (mola vermek: to take a break)
to make it in time; to catch (a bus, a train: dative)
to get dark (hava kararıyor: it's getting dark)

exercises.explain: `-(y)IncA` starts with a vowel, so *git-* softens to *gid-*. Its vowel i is front, so *-ince*: *gidince*.

exercises.question: How do you say **I'll call you when I get home**?

why.1: *Gelirken* is **on the way home**, while still coming. Once you're home: `-(y)IncA`.
why.2: *Aradım* is the past: **when I got home, I called you**. The main verb carries the tense.

exercises.explain: *gel-ince*, **when I get home**; the aorist *ararım* makes it a promise for later.

exercises.en: When the lesson was over, we went to a café.

accept: ince

reject.why: Harmony: *bit-* has i, a front vowel, so *-ince*.
*Biterken* is **as it was ending**. The lesson was over: `-(y)IncA`, *bitince*.

exercises.explain: *bit-ince*: once the lesson had ended, the next thing happened.

accept: When I get to the bus station, I will text you.
When I get to the bus station, I will [send you a message|message you|send you a text].
When I [reach|arrive at] the bus station, I will [text you|send you a message|message you|send you a text].
When I [get to|reach|arrive at] the [coach station|bus terminal], I will [text you|send you a message|message you|send you a text].
Once I [get to|reach|arrive at] the [bus station|coach station|bus terminal], I will [text you|send you a message|message you|send you a text].
I will [text you|send you a message|message you|send you a text] [when|once] I [get to|reach|arrive at] the [bus station|coach station|bus terminal].

exercises.prompt: When the bus came, we got on.
accept: Otobüs gelince bindik.
Otobüs gelince biz bindik.
Biz otobüs gelince bindik.

reject.why: *Gelirken* is **while it was coming**: you can't get on yet. Once it has come: *Otobüs gelince*.

exercises.en: When it got dark, we went back home.
We'll wait here until you come.

exercises.prompt: We'll take a break when we reach Izmir.
Wait here until I come back.
accept: Ben dönünceye kadar burada bekle.
Ben dönünceye kadar burada [bekleyin|bekleyiniz].
Ben [geri gelinceye|gelinceye|dönene|geri gelene|gelene] kadar burada [bekle|bekleyin|bekleyiniz].
[Dönünceye|Geri gelinceye|Gelinceye|Dönene|Geri gelene|Gelene] kadar burada [bekle|bekleyin|bekleyiniz].

reject.why: *Dönünce* is **when I come back**. For **until**, add the dative and *kadar*: *dönünceye kadar*.

exercises.en: When evening came, we set off.

exercises.question: *Otobüs gelmeyince yürüdük.* What happened?
options: The bus didn't come, so we walked.
We walked until the bus came.
We walked, and then the bus came.

why.2: *Gelmeyince* is negative: the bus never came.

exercises.explain: *gel-me-y-ince*: the negative `-mA` + `-(y)IncA`, **when it didn't come**. The negative form usually gives a reason.

accept: When I could not catch the bus, I took a taxi.
When I [missed|did not catch|could not make] the bus, I [took|got|caught] a [taxi|cab].
When I could not catch the bus, I [got|caught] a [taxi|cab].
When I could not catch the bus, I took a cab.
[Because|Since|As] I [could not catch|missed|did not catch|could not make] the bus, I [took|got|caught] a [taxi|cab].
I [took|got|caught] a [taxi|cab] [when|because|since] I [could not catch|missed|did not catch|could not make] the bus.
I [missed|could not catch] the bus, so I [took|got|caught] a [taxi|cab].
